meta.note: connected_now reflects the MCP server list a live session declared on connected_verified. Probes re-run on every dashboard refresh.

tools.name: Issue tracker (MCP connector)

alternatives.what: the tracker's CLI, which works unattended

tools.fix: OAuth connector — reconnect it in the desktop app. It is absent from headless and cron runs by design, which is what the CLI entry is for.
tools.notes: An OAuth connector has nothing checkable from a shell, so it reports on connected_now plus its transcript history rather than a fabricated probe.

tools.name: Issue tracker (CLI)
tools.access: CLI · installed binary, token in the keyring
tools.fix: Run the tool's own auth login against the right host. Check the version too — an outdated client fails in ways that read like permission errors.
tools.probe: command -v tracker >/dev/null && tracker --version 2>&1 | head -1 || echo FAIL
tools.notes: The automation-safe path. Prefer it over the connector for anything scheduled.

tools.name: Nightly sync (scheduled)
tools.fix: Re-run the installer after any machine wipe. A LaunchAgent that was never loaded fails exactly like one with nothing to do, which is why this entry exists at all.
tools.probe: launchctl list 2>/dev/null | grep -q nightly-sync && echo loaded || echo FAIL
tools.notes: depends_on means a broken CLI downgrades this to degraded even when the agent itself is loaded and running.
